titel: Hotel near Mind Mystery | Hotel Asteria Venray
omschrijving: Mind Mystery in Horst is a 10-minute drive from Hotel Asteria in Venray. What you will experience there, and how to end the day with wellness and dinner.
hero-sub: An experience museum full of optical illusions in Horst, a ten-minute drive from your hotel room in Venray.
hero-alt: Hotel Asteria in Venray with the pond and fountain in front
t3-waarde: Wed and Fri 11 am-5 pm, Sat and Sun 10 am-5 pm (Nov 2026)
v1-p1: Mind Mystery in Horst is a ten-minute drive from Hotel Asteria. It is an experience museum, partly indoors and partly outdoors, where everything revolves around optical illusions: what your eyes see and what your brain makes of it. The park opened in 2018 and is compact, with a lot to see in a small space.
v1-p2: You walk through the Upside Down House, where the furniture is fixed to the ceiling, and across the bridge of the Vortex, a rotating tunnel in which walking in a straight line suddenly becomes tricky. In the Ames Room you grow tall or shrink, and the mirror maze is full of mirrors and small dilemmas to talk over together.
v1-alt: The 1915 drawing My Wife and My Mother-in-Law: you see either a young woman looking away or an old woman with a large nose
v2-kop: A museum full of double images
v2-p1: The museum, spread over five rooms, displays graphic illusions with an explanation of each. Many are ambiguous figures, such as the drawing of a rabbit that is also a duck, first published in 1892. In the 3D room you put on glasses and the paintings come out towards you.
v2-p2: Outside, a terrace with puzzles and brain teasers awaits. There are four automatic photo points and plenty of spots where you can take your own pictures. In the café you can have a filled roll or a slice of Limburgse vlaai, the regional fruit tart.
v2-alt: An 1892 drawing of an animal you can see as a rabbit or a duck, captioned Kaninchen und Ente
v3-p1: Most of Mind Mystery is indoors; only the paths between the attractions and the puzzle terrace are outside. That makes it a good choice for a grey day. If you have time left, drive on for a quarter of an hour to Arcen for a guided tour of the Hertog Jan Brewery. From there you are back in Venray within half an hour, where the sauna on the Top Floor is waiting for you.
v3-alt: The Top Floor wellness area at Hotel Asteria in Venray, with a round foot bath and large plants
tip: Book a time slot at the start of the day. That way you are back outside after two to three hours, in plenty of time for the sauna. If you can choose, go on a weekday: outside the school holidays it is quieter and you get €2 off each ticket. Parking is free right outside the door. And charge your phone before you go: in the Ames Room and the Upside Down House you will take more photos than you think.
g1-tekst: In November 2026 on Wednesdays and Fridays from 11 am to 5 pm and at weekends from 10 am to 5 pm. Closed on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays. Check your day on mindmystery.nl.
g1-alt: A Penrose triangle: three bars that together form an impossible triangle
g2-tekst: €18.95 per person, children aged 5 to 11 €14.95, children up to 4 free. €2 off on weekdays outside the school holidays.
g2-alt: Drawing of an animal's head: with the beak to the left a duck, with the ears to the left a rabbit
g3-tekst: Parking is free, right by the entrance. From junction 10 of the A73 it is less than a minute's drive.
g3-alt: Detail of a 1915 drawing of a woman in profile, whom you can also see as an old woman
g4-tekst: Dogs are not allowed inside. Assistance and guide dogs are welcome.
g4-alt: Vase-or-faces illusion: a vase or two faces looking at each other, as at Mind Mystery in Horst
dag-kop: How to make a day of it
dag-sub: Breakfast at the hotel, a day of having your brain fooled in Horst, and back in the late afternoon for the sauna and dinner.
m1-tekst: The breakfast buffet is served from 7 am to 10 am on weekdays and from 8 am to 10.30 am at weekends. Then you get in the car: ten minutes later you are in Horst.
m1-alt: Basket of fresh bread rolls on the breakfast buffet at Hotel Asteria in Venray
m2-tekst: Allow two to three hours for the Upside Down House, the Vortex, the mirror maze and the museum. Have lunch in the café with a roll or a slice of vlaai.
m2-alt: A 1915 drawing of a woman with a feather in her hat: a young woman or an old one
m3-tekst: Back in Venray, let your mind settle in the sauna. The wellness area is open from Monday to Thursday from 4 pm to 10 pm and from Friday to Sunday from 12 noon to 10 pm. Tuesday is swimwear day.
m3-alt: Foot bath with green mosaic tiles under a skylight in the Top Floor wellness area at Hotel Asteria
m4-tekst: End the day at a table in the hotel's brasserie. The kitchen is open until 9.30 pm, and afterwards your room is just a lift ride away.
m4-alt: Bartender pulling a beer at the brasserie bar in Hotel Asteria, Venray
kamers-sub: After a day full of illusions, a proper bed is a welcome thought. Choose your room; you will see the price for your dates straight away when you book.
kaart-regel: Mind Mystery lies south of Venray, on the edge of Horst and close to the A73. The map also shows three other days out near the hotel.
kaart-alt: Map of North Limburg with Hotel Asteria in Venray, Mind Mystery in Horst and three other days out
f1-v: How far is Mind Mystery from Hotel Asteria?
f1-a: It is 11.2 kilometres, about 10 minutes by car. By bike it is 10.7 kilometres, around 45 minutes. You can hire bikes and e-bikes at our reception.
f2-v: How long does a visit to Mind Mystery take?
f2-a: According to Mind Mystery, a visit takes two to three hours on average, depending on your pace and how long you spend on the puzzles. You can stay as long as you like.
f3-v: Is Mind Mystery worth visiting when it rains?
f3-a: Yes. Most of it is indoors, such as the Upside Down House, the mirror maze and the museum. Only the paths between the attractions and the puzzle terrace are outside.
f4-v: Should I buy tickets in advance?
f4-a: That is a good idea. Mind Mystery works with time slots and can sell out at weekends and in the holidays. A ticket costs €18.95, or €14.95 for children aged 5 to 11 (November 2026). You show the QR code on your phone, and changing to another day is free as long as there is space.
f5-v: Can I bring my dog to Mind Mystery?
f5-a: No, dogs are not allowed. Assistance and guide dogs are welcome.
f6-v: Can I still use the wellness area and have dinner at the hotel after Mind Mystery?
f6-a: Yes. The wellness area is open from Monday to Thursday from 4 pm to 10 pm and from Friday to Sunday from 12 noon to 10 pm. Tuesday is swimwear day. You can have dinner in the brasserie until 9.30 pm.

oorlogsmuseum.desc: After the illusions of Mind Mystery, this is a day out with both feet firmly in reality. In Overloon a large museum tells the story of the Second World War, with military vehicles in reconstructed scenes and a Sherman tank outside. It is a ten-minute drive from the hotel, and here too you are mostly indoors.

maasduinen.desc: If you would rather head outdoors after an afternoon inside, more than 4,500 hectares of woodland, heath, drift sand and fens lie between the River Maas and the German border: the longest belt of river dunes in the Netherlands. At the visitor centre in Well you will find walking and cycling routes. Back at the hotel, the sauna on the Top Floor is waiting.
maasduinen.credit: Photos: Lieblingsgouda, Steven Lek, Carelbullens and Jonathation via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA), cropped.

hertogjan.desc: In Arcen, a quarter of an hour from Mind Mystery, Hertog Jan brews its beer. On a guided tour you see how the brewing is done, smell the hops and taste the malt and the beer. Book the tour in advance and bear in mind the narrow corridors and 144 steps.
hertogjan.credit: Photos: B. Hulshoff and Steven Lek via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped; photo of the tap: Hotel Asteria.
